**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — LICENSE, paragraph 2 (p0002)**

The Kubient licence grant falls short of our playbook position in three ways:

1. **No affiliate/contractor coverage** — the grant runs to "Customer" alone, even though AP affiliates and third-party contractors operate our ad stack and would need to access the Auction Platform.
2. **Revocable at will** — the grant is expressly "revocable," which lets Kubient cut off platform access outside any termination event. Paragraph 4 already sets out termination (including 30-day cure for material breach), so revocability should be tied to that.
3. **Non-transferable / non-assignable** — this conflicts with paragraph 14(h), which the parties agreed permits assignment to an affiliate, an asset purchaser, or a successor by merger; the licence itself would not follow such an assignment.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** amended p0002 to grant the licence to Customer, its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf; deleted "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable"; made the licence transferable with a permitted assignment under paragraph 14(h) and sublicensable to those affiliates/contractors; and limited revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4.

Fallback offered in the comment: affiliate coverage on written notice to Kubient, with transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction.
